headline: Explosions hit Riyadh as King Khalid Airport partially reopens
summary: Riyadh's international airport resumed flights after a two-week closure, but Houthi rebels warn the facility remains a military target.
details: Explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Sunday as King Khalid International Airport partially reopened after a two-week closure following Houthi strikes.
The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting and destroying a ballistic missile and two drones launched by the Iran-backed Houthi militia toward Riyadh.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that the airport is still 'unsafe' and a 'military target,' urging airlines and travelers to avoid the facility.
The reopening comes after a devastating attack earlier this month that killed 13 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest strike in the kingdom in over a decade.
Residents in the capital received alert messages for a 'hostile aerial threat,' urging them to stay in safe locations during the early hours of Sunday.
The conflict has escalated after a truce between the Houthis and the Riyadh-backed government in Yemen collapsed, further destabilizing the region and disrupting oil markets.

caption:
Explosions in Riyadh as the city's main airport reopens after two weeks of closure. Are travelers safe?

Explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Sunday as King Khalid International Airport partially reopened after a two-week closure following Houthi strikes.

The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting and destroying a ballistic missile and two drones launched by the Iran-backed Houthi militia toward Riyadh.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that the airport is still 'unsafe' and a 'military target,' urging airlines and travelers to avoid the facility.

The reopening comes after a devastating attack earlier this month that killed 13 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest strike in the kingdom in over a decade.

Residents in the capital received alert messages for a 'hostile aerial threat,' urging them to stay in safe locations during the early hours of Sunday.

The conflict has escalated after a truce between the Houthis and the Riyadh-backed government in Yemen collapsed, further destabilizing the region and disrupting oil markets.

Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter, has seen its businesses and airlines disrupted by the ongoing barrage of strikes from the Houthi group.

headline_marked: 100 sued as [[anti-terror case filed over police attack]] in Gopalganj
headline: 100 sued as anti-terror case filed over police attack in Gopalganj
summary: Seven people have been arrested after activists of banned Awami League associate organisations attacked on-duty police and vandalised a vehicle.
details: A case has been filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act following an attack on police and the vandalism of a police vehicle during a rally in Gopalganj.
The incident occurred around Saturday noon at Raghunathpur Ferry Ghat, where activists of banned associate organisations of the Awami League attacked on-duty officers.
Two police personnel, including a sub-inspector, were injured during the clash. The case was filed by the injured Sub-Inspector Md Ful Mia Khan.
The lawsuit names 40 specific accused and lists another 50 to 60 unidentified persons, bringing the total to around 100 people.
Following the attack, police conducted raids across the district and detained 30 individuals for questioning.
After verification, 23 people were released, while seven were formally arrested and sent to jail after appearing before a court.
Gopalganj Superintendent of Police Md Habibullah confirmed the details of the case and the arrests to the media.
caption:
100 people sued under the Anti-Terrorism Act after a violent attack on police in Gopalganj.

A case has been filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act following an attack on police and the vandalism of a police vehicle during a rally in Gopalganj.

The incident occurred around Saturday noon at Raghunathpur Ferry Ghat, where activists of banned associate organisations of the Awami League attacked on-duty officers.

Two police personnel, including a sub-inspector, were injured during the clash. The case was filed by the injured Sub-Inspector Md Ful Mia Khan.

The lawsuit names 40 specific accused and lists another 50 to 60 unidentified persons, bringing the total to around 100 people.

Following the attack, police conducted raids across the district and detained 30 individuals for questioning.

After verification, 23 people were released, while seven were formally arrested and sent to jail after appearing before a court.

Gopalganj Superintendent of Police Md Habibullah confirmed the details of the case and the arrests to the media.
